title: Transactional Outbox That Survives Crashes
signature: def place_order(db, order) -> str; def relay(db, broker) -> int; class RevenueConsumer: __init__(store), handle(message) -> str
hints: The order row and its outbox row go in one transaction with one commit. Two commits leave a crash window where the order exists and its event never will.
The relay publishes first and marks the row published afterwards. A crash in between republishes the event (fine, the consumer dedupes); the other order loses it.
Retries happen: the client resends after a lost response, and the broker redelivers after a lost ack. Make place_order a no-op for an existing order_id.
The consumer's dedupe marker and its revenue update must commit in the same transaction in the consumer's store. A Python set dies with the process.
